verdicts.correction: On the OSWorld 2.1 strict-pass chart, Haiku 5.5 at max effort (about 37% at about $0.61 per task) sits above Sonnet 5.5's three lowest effort points (about 24%, 30% and 35%) and Opus 5.5's lowest (about 29%) while costing less per task than any Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 point (cheapest Sonnet 5.5 point about $0.68, cheapest Opus 5.5 point about $0.98); it is below Sonnet 5.5's top two points (about 45% and 49%) and Opus 5.5's top four (about 43%, 46%, 51%, 53%) (read from chart).
verdicts.why: Sonnet 5.5's third point measures about 35.3% (marker centroid), which is below Haiku 5.5's max point at about 37.1%, so Haiku 5.5 max beats three Sonnet 5.5 effort points, not two.

verdicts.correction: The OfficeQA evaluation was run agentically with the relevant documents preselected and provided as extracted text; the page does not itself say what this excludes (that it leaves out the model's own retrieval of documents from the corpus is a reader's inference).
verdicts.why: The clause 'so it does not test the model's own retrieval' is an inference, not a statement on page 130.

verdicts.correction: Biomedical image analysis chart labels (score 0-1): Gemini 3.8 Flash 0.55; GPT-6 Luna 0.47; Claude Sonnet 5 0.42; Claude Opus 5.5 0.71; Claude Sonnet 5.5 0.72; Claude Haiku 5.5 0.44. This is the panel where Haiku 5.5 trails Sonnet 5.5 by the most (0.28); its gap to Opus 5.5 here (0.27) is the same size as its gap to Opus 5.5 on protein Sequence generation (0.60 vs 0.33 = 0.27). Haiku 5.5's label is also below Gemini 3.8 Flash (0.55) and GPT-6 Luna (0.47), but the drawn error bars of Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 3.8 Flash overlap (this benchmark ran 1 attempt per problem).
verdicts.why: The 'trails by the most' claim holds for Sonnet 5.5 but only ties for Opus 5.5 (Sequence generation gap is also 0.27), and the below-Luna/Gemini ordering is inside overlapping error bars.
